title: feat(sync): keep the Mac awake for the length of a run
body:
## Summary
A full 18-step report run takes about 20 minutes of step time. On 2026-09-22 a laptop slept partway through one: `access` failed on an expired Google session, and the run took four hours of wall clock. On macOS the runner now keeps the Mac awake for as long as the run lasts. It also documents what "sync" means: all 18 steps, straight through.

## Changesets

### 1. `feat(sync): keep the Mac awake for the length of a run`
**Files:** `skills/aaif-sync/scripts/sync.py`, `skills/aaif-sync/scripts/test_sync.py`, `skills/aaif-sync/SKILL.md` (+43)
- `keep_awake()` starts `caffeinate -i -w <runner pid>`. It stops on its own when the runner exits, whether the run finishes, crashes or is interrupted. Nothing is spawned off macOS, or on a Mac without `caffeinate`. `nightly.py` goes through `sync.main`, so it gets the same behaviour.
- `sync.py` stays lib-free: it uses only `shutil.which` and `subprocess.Popen`.
- The skill's "Run it" step now says the default run is the whole pipeline, never narrowed to save time.

## Test Plan
- [x] `test_sync.py`: on macOS the right `caffeinate` argv is spawned, nothing is spawned off macOS, and a Mac without `caffeinate` still runs. Every other `main()` test runs with `keep_awake` stubbed out.
- [x] `PYTHONPATH=lib python -m pytest lib/aaif_events/tests -q` passes, and so does pre-commit.
- [x] Live: a full 18-step report run finished in 11.5 min of wall clock, with no sleep and no failed step.
